SECTION l: DATA COLLECTION TECHNIQUE
This section provides information regarding the purpose of publication, data
collection procedure, statistical tools, presentation of data, data limitations, and
implications.
PURPOSE OF THE PUBLICATION:
The Bureau of Police Research & Development has been publishing the “Data on
Police Organizations” in India since 1986, annually. From time to time, some of the
essential features like women police, police expenditure, constabulary ratio, transport
facilities, communication facilities, representation of SCs/STs, and police training
institutes were added.
```
In this publication, dimensions like the infrastructure of CAPFs (vehicle availability,
```
```
family quarters, training institutions, tracker and sniffer dogs, and pay scales), Gender-
```
wise data on Police Forces, District Armed Reserve Police, Senior Supervisory Officers,
Immediate Supervisory Officers, and Field Staff Ratio, Data of Women Police, Sanctioned
and Actual Strength of SCs/STs and OBCs have been added.
This issue of “Data on Police Organizations” in India, as on 01.01.2024, will be more
beneficial for the users, especially for the policymakers, police officers, researchers,
academicians, police administrators, and other stakeholders.
DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURE:
```
“Data on Police Organizations” in India (DoPO) has been prepared based on the
```
data provided by the States/UTs, CAPFs, and other Central Police Organizations. Further,
```
data have also been obtained from the Registrar General of India (RGI) and the Survey
```
of India.
INTRODUCTION
Promoting Good Practices and Standards
4
STATISTICAL TOOLS:
Statistical methods involved in carrying out the study include planning, designing,
collecting data, analyzing, drawing meaningful interpretation, and reporting the
findings.
PRESENTATION OF DATA:
Data is collected in a raw format. Therefore, it has been summarized, processed,
analyzed, and presented in charts and tables to make it more meaningful. However,
even in this format, there are inherent difficulties in its understanding.
The graph is a very effective visual tool. It displays data at a glance, facilitates
comparison, reveals trends and relationships within the data, such as changes over time,
frequency distribution and correlation, etc. Bar graphs, Pie charts, and other statistical
tools have been used.
DATA LIMITATIONS:
DoPO has been prepared based on data provided by the States/UTs/CAPFs and
other Police Organizations.
Police structures in different States/UTs, CAPFs, and CPOs are not uniform. In a few
```
cases, States/UTs have not provided complete data; therefore, it has been mentioned
```
```
as (NA) which denotes “Not Available”, (NP) denotes “Not Provided”, whereas (-) denotes
```
“Zero” in the relevant Tables. Wherever appropriate, data of the previous year has been
incorporated for the sake of comparison.
Promoting Good Practices and Standards
5
SECTION II: INDIAN DEMOGRAPHY
 Male & Female Population
 Geographical Area
This section depicts the information/data of States/UTs regarding demography,
containing the country’s male-female population and geographical area.
MALE & FEMALE POPULATION:
Demography is the statistical study of populations. At a glance, it analyzes living
population, i.e., human changes over time and space in response to birth, migration,
aging, death, etc.
Its analysis covers entire society or groups defined by education, nationality, religion,
ethnicity, etc. Demographic studies also analyze the relationships between economic,
social, cultural, and biological processes influencing the population.
The total population of India, as on 01.10.2023, as provided by the Registrar General
of India and the Census Commissioner of India, is 139.54 crore, approx., comprising
71.68 crore males and 67.86 crore females.
Among the States, Uttar Pradesh, with a population of more than 23.70 crore, is the
most populous state in the country, followed by Bihar, with a population of 12.78 crore.
Among the Union Territories, Delhi, with a population of more than 2.15 crore, is the
most populous UT in the country, followed by J&K, with a population of 1.36 crore.
GEOGRAPHICAL AREA:
The total geographical area of the country is 32,87,470 Sq. Km., approximately.
In terms of geographical area, the largest state in India is Rajasthan, with an area of
3,42,239 Sq. Km. and the smallest is the UT of Lakshadweep, with an area of 30 Sq. Km.

District Armed Reserve Police, State Special Armed Police and the total strength of Police.

```
been provided. Officers to Field Staff Ratio (Teeth to Tail Ratio) has been computed for
```
sanctioned and actual police strength of States/UTs. Efforts have been made to provide
rank wise sanctioned and actual strength of Traffic Police, Special Branch, CID/Crime
Branch and Special Police Units.

lakh of the total police force in the country, 19.31 lakh are Civil Police, 2.71 lakh are
```
District Armed Reserve Police and the remaining 3.88+1.65 (lRBn) lakh, are State Special
```
```
Armed Police. The total sanctioned strength is the highest in Uttar Pradesh (4.29 lakh),
```

```
followed by Maharashtra (2.37 lakh).
```

```
(55,913), followed by Tamil Nadu (32,190).
```

```
(2.07 lakh).
```

relative strength of police personnel in different ranks. It also helps Police Organizations
in preparing management plan of the Police forces, generally, comparing Senior

```
Supervisory Officers (Dy.SP to DG) and Immediate Supervisory Officers (Inspector to
```
```
ASI) with field personnel (Head Constable and Constable).
```

```
(approx.). (Table No- 3.1.5) as also shown in the chart below.
```

SECTION III : WOMEN IN POLICE
Availability of adequate number of women in police is essential for reducing the
vulnerability of women against crimes. The existing Women Police Population Ratio is
still very low. Poor representation of women in police is posing serious challenges in
dealing with crimes against women and women criminals. Therefore, it is essential that
women Police personnel are visible at the cutting edge level.

UTs of A&N Islands, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Delhi,
Lakshadweep and Puducherry are directly financed by the Ministry of Home Affairs,
Government of India.
EXPENDITURE OF STATE/UT POLICE FORCES
The sanctioned strength of State Police Forces has increased to 27.55 lakh in 2023
over 27.22 lakh in 2022 and the expenditure on State Police Forces has increased to
```
₹1,87,271.97 crore in the year 2023-24 (Tentative), from ₹1,79,143.57 crore in the year
```
```
2022-23 (Revised) (Table No - 4.1.3).
```
EXPENDITURE ON POLICE TRAINING
An amount of ₹2,500.60 crore was spent on police training at the all India level
in the year 2023-24, out of the total police expenditure of ₹1,87,271.97 crore during
the same year. The maximum expenditure on training, i.e ₹745.25 crore, was made by
```
Uttar Pradesh (Table No - 4.1.3).
```
TRENDS IN POLICE TRAINING EXPENDITURE
Expenditure on Police Training from 2015-16 to 2023-24 has shown mixed
trends. It increased from 2015-16 to 2018-19 and slightly decreased in 2019-20 and
increased in 2020-21 but slightly decreased in 2021-22 and again increased in 2022-23
to 2023-24 as shown in the graph given below:-

MODERNIZATION GRANTS TO THE STATE POLICE FORCES
Modernization grants to the state police forces, allocated by the MHA, are meant
to upgrade the infrastructure of the state police in order to improve their capacity to
meet the emerging challenges of internal security, besides improving efficiency and
effectiveness in Police service delivery.
The focus of the scheme is on strengthening of the police infrastructure by way
of construction of secure and people friendly Police Stations, Police Outposts, Police
Housing, improved Mobility, Modern Weaponry, Computerization, Communication
Equipment, Modern Traffic Control Equipment, etc.
At the national level, the grants made available to the state police forces in the
financial year 2023-24 by the Central Government and the State Governments and the
total amount utilized for modernization by the State Governments for the State Police
```
Forces are given at Table No - 4.1.4 (B).

```

An analysis of the data on police administrative offices shows that the country is
divided into 87 Police Zones, 197 Police Ranges covering 848 Police Districts, 2,335
Police Sub-Divisions, and 1,906 Police Circles. There are 18,284 sanctioned Police
Stations in the country. Tamil Nadu has the highest sanctioned number of Police
Stations in the country i.e., 2,349, whereas the lowest, i.e., 11 Police Stations, are in
```
Ladakh (Table No - 5.1.1).
```

POLICE STATIONS
Out of the 18,284 sanctioned Police Stations, 9,127 Police Stations are located in
rural areas, whereas 5,492 Police Stations are located in urban areas, and the remaining

```
3,665 are the Special Purpose Police Stations (Table No - 5.1.2) and shown in the graph
```
at the end of this section.
POLICE POSTS
Data on the sanctioned Police Posts/Outposts reveals that, out of the total of 9,301
Police Posts in the country, 5,216 Police Posts are located in Rural areas, whereas 3,278
Police Posts are located in Urban areas. The remaining 807 Police Posts are Railways
```
Police Posts etc. (Table No - 5.1.3.)
```

SECTION II : TRANSPORT FACILITIES
```
Data have been compiled about different types of transport facilities (vehicles)
```
available with the police force in the States/UTs Police and CAPFs. The number of vehicles
available per 100 police Personnel has also been calculated.
```
TRANSPORT FACILITIES (MOBILITY)
```
Mobility is measured in terms of the availability of vehicles to move the unit on the
call of duty. Police mobility is directly linked with its operational efficiency. During law
and order situations, the quick response of police forces helps significantly in protecting
the life and property of the people.
Vehicles required to provide mobility to Police Forces have been divided into four
```
categories, i.e., Heavy Vehicles (buses/trucks, troop carriers, etc.), Medium Vehicles,
```
```
Light Vehicles (jeeps/cars, etc.), and Very Light Vehicles (three/two Wheelers). Heavy,
```
Medium and Light vehicles cater to the requirements of the Police Stations and field-
level supervisory and senior supervisory officers.
Besides above, State Police have also procured some special purpose vehicles: like
```
Mines Protected Vehicles (MPV), Riot Control Vehicles, Ambulances, Mobile Forensic
```
Vans, Water Cannons, Water Tankers, Prison Vans, etc., to meet their specific needs. These
vehicles have been clubbed under the “ Other Category
```
In all, 2,42,065 vehicles were available with State/UT Police Force in 2023 ; This
```
number increased from 2,35,076 during 2022. Out of 2,42,065 vehicles, 11,377 are Heavy
duty Vehicles, 18,799 Medium-duty Vehicles, 98,250 Light Vehicles, 1,10,770 Very Light
```
Vehicles (two/three-wheelers) and 2,869 are Other Vehicles (Table No-5.1.6).
```
NUMBER OF VEHICLES PER 100 POLICE PERSONNEL
```
Transport facility (no. of vehicles) available per 100 sanctioned police personnel was
```
8.79 in 2023 at the national level, which has increased from 8.63 in the previous year
```
(Table No - 5.1.7). However, the actual availability is 11.19.
```

SECTION l: EQUIPMENT TO FACILITATE POLICING
This section provides State/UT wise data on CCTV cameras, computers, servers
and laptops, speedometers, breath analyzers, and forensic science laboratories/mobile
forensic science vans available with the Police.
Police human resources alone are insufficient to curb crime, maintain law and order,
traffic management, internal security, and other policing requirements. Therefore,
they must be supplemented with modern facilities and gadgets like computers, CCTV
cameras, traffic and investigation equipment, speedometers, breath analyzers, forensic
science kits/labs, etc., to enhance effectiveness and efficiency.

SECTION II: TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT
This section contains the data from States/UTs in respect of Police Personnel
```
(Constables and SIs) recruited during the year 2023 and the number of newly recruited
```
police personnel who underwent training.
POLICE PERSONNEL RECRUITED
The 49,233 Police Constables were recruited during 2023 against the 63,656
recruited in 2022. At the State level, the highest number of 13,953 Constables were
```
recruited in Telangana, followed by 5,395 in Haryana (Table No - 6.1.8).
```
```
The number of Sub-Inspectors (SIs) recruited during 2023 was 10,332, whereas this
```
figure was 16,802, during 2022. At the State level, the highest number of SIs recruited
```
were 5971 in Bihar, followed by 1,155 in West Bengal (Table No - 6.1.8).
```
IPS OFFICERS
The sanctioned strength of IPS Officers, as on 01.01.2024, was 5,055 at the all- India
level, whereas 4,469 officers are available. Further, 504 IPS Officers were on deputation
```
with the Central Government (Table No - 6.2.2).
```
POLICE TRAINING INSTITUTES
Regular and adequate training of Police Personnel at all levels is necessary to
upgrade their professional knowledge, skills, and attitude and instill confidence and
professionalism in the Police Personnel. It contains information about Police Training
Institutes of the States/ UTs and CAPFs. These institutions cater to the basic training
of the newly recruited Police Personnel, in-service training to Police Personnel of
different ranks: specialized training to the Police Personnel deployed for specialized
```
work and assignments like Special Task Force (STF), Special Investigation Teams
```
```
(SITs), Commandos, etc. Some of these training institutes have been recognized
```
as the “Centre of Excellence” for imparting specialized training in a particular
field/ craft/ trade.


@ There is no separate sanctioned strength for female in CISF. Hence, included females strength in above.
# No reservation in respect of women has been approved by the GOI. However, as per MHA ID No 45015/16/2015/Pers-1 dated 05.01.2016, representation
```
of women is required to be enhanced to 14-15% posts at Constable level in border guarding force (i.e. ITBP). For this purpose, 15% vacancies in ITBP
```

are being kept reserved for women in the direct recruitment for NGO’s in all cadres.
